name: Message Gate
info:
# 🚦 Message Gate Subflow

## 🧠 Function

This subflow provides a reusable persistent **pass/block message gate**.

It can be used to enable or disable message flow using:

* Dashboard switch
* Inject node
* MQTT command
* Function node
* Any flow that sends a boolean control message

The gate stores its state persistently and decides whether incoming messages are passed or silently blocked.

---

## 📥 Input

The subflow has **one input**.

Incoming messages are interpreted in two ways:

---

## 🎛 Control Messages

The gate can be enabled or disabled using:

```javascript
msg.enable = true;
```

or:

```javascript
msg.enable = false;
```

Alternative dashboard/MQTT-friendly format:

```javascript
msg.topic = "enable";
msg.payload = true;
```

or:

```javascript
msg.topic = "enable";
msg.payload = false;
```

### Meaning

| Message                                        | Function     |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| `msg.enable = true`                            | Enable gate  |
| `msg.enable = false`                           | Disable gate |
| `msg.topic = "enable"` + `msg.payload = true`  | Enable gate  |
| `msg.topic = "enable"` + `msg.payload = false` | Disable gate |

Control messages are **not passed through Output 1**.

---

## 📩 Normal Messages

Any message that is **not** a control message is treated as a normal message.

If the gate is enabled:

```text
message passes
```

If the gate is disabled:

```text
message is blocked
```

The original message is passed unchanged.

---

## 📤 Outputs

### Output 1 — Passed Messages

Only messages that pass the gate.

```javascript
msg // original message, unchanged
```

If the gate is disabled, no message is sent.

---

### Output 2 — Gate State

Emits only when the gate state changes.

```javascript
msg.payload = true | false
msg.topic = stateName
```

Additional metadata:

```javascript
msg.gate = {
    name: stateName,
    label: label,
    enabled: true | false
};
```

---

## ⚙️ Environment Variables

### stateName

Name of the persistent flow variable.

Example:

```text
notificationGate
```

Stored as:

```javascript
flow.get(stateName, "file")
flow.set(stateName, value, "file")
```

---

### default

Initial state when the persistent variable does not yet exist.

Default:

```text
true
```

---

### label

Human-readable label used in metadata.

Example:

```text
Notification Gate
```

---

## 📌 Status Indicator

The subflow displays its current state on the Node-RED workspace.

| Status     | Meaning              |
| ---------- | -------------------- |
| 🟢 ENABLED | Messages are passed  |
| 🔴 BLOCKED | Messages are blocked |

---

## 🚀 Usage Example

### Dashboard switch

Configure a `ui_switch` as:

```text
topic: enable
on payload: true
off payload: false
```

Wire it directly into the Message Gate.

---

### Notification example

```text
Rain Alert
    │
    ▼
Message Gate
    │
    ▼
HA+WA Notification
```

When the gate is enabled, alerts are sent.

When the gate is disabled, alerts are suppressed.

---

## 🧩 Design Goals

* One input, suitable for Node-RED subflows
* Minimal wiring
* Persistent enable/disable state
* Dashboard-friendly control
* Original messages pass unchanged
* Blocked messages are silently discarded
* State changes are available on Output 2
* Easy to reuse across many flows

---

## Typical Applications

* Enable/disable notifications
* Maintenance mode gate
* Alarm message filter
* Doorbell mute
* Rain alert mute
* Debug/test mode switch
* Temporarily block MQTT messages
* Disable non-critical automations

---

## Design Notes

* The subflow deliberately does **not** output blocked messages.
* Output 2 is used for gate state feedback.
* Control messages are consumed by the gate.
* Normal messages are never modified.
* State is stored persistently using **flow context (`file`)**.

# 📡 HA + WhatsApp Notification Subflow

## 🧠 Function
This subflow provides a unified notification system for:

- Home Assistant Mobile App
- WhatsApp (see [github](https://github.com/raulpetruta/ha-wa-bridge ))

It accepts a structured alert object and automatically formats and routes it to all configured channels.

---

## 📥 Input

The subflow expects an alert object on:

msg.alert

### Structure
```js
msg.alert = {
    title: "Alert title",
    message: "Main alert message",
    severity: "info | warning | critical",
    source: "sensor or system name",
    timestamp: "optional",
    
    notify: {
        ha: true,
        whatsapp: true
    }
};
```
---

## 🔁 Fallback behavior

If msg.alert is missing, the subflow will use:

- msg.payload.message
- severity = "info"

---

## 🎨 Message format

All notifications are formatted as:

[emoji] [source] message

### Examples:
ℹ️ [system] Everything is OK  
⚠️ [rain_sensor] Heavy rain detected  
🚨 [freezer] Temperature critical  

---

## 📤 Output channels

### WhatsApp
- Sends formatted message to configured number
- Optimized for short alert messages

### Home Assistant Mobile App
- Sends push notification via notify.mobile_app_*
- Uses:
  - title = alert.title
  - message = formatted message

---

## ⚙️ Configuration

Stored in:

flow.get("notification")

Example initialization:

flow.set("notification", {
    whatsapp: "31621201520",
    mobile: "mobile_app_iphone13mini_van_roland"
});

---

## 🚀 Usage

Create an alert:

msg.alert = {
    title: "Rain Alert",
    message: "Heavy rain expected",
    severity: "warning",
    source: "weather_station"
};

return msg;

Then pass it into this subflow.

---

## 🧩 Design goals

- Centralized notification logic
- Consistent formatting across channels
- Easy to extend (Telegram, MQTT, email)
- Reusable across all flows
- Separation of alert creation and delivery

info:
# ☀️ SunRain Shades

**Project:** myHome  
**Flow:** SunRain Shades  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Author:** Roland van Dalen  
**Last Updated:** 2026-07-04

---

# 🧠 Overview

This flow provides complete monitoring, manual control and weather protection for the **SunRain Somfy RTS awning**.

The awning is controlled by an **ESPSomfy RTS** controller using MQTT, while a **HomeWizard Energy Socket** is used to determine whether the motor is running.

A **Buienradar** rain forecast is continuously monitored to warn when rain is approaching. Rain notifications are automatically suppressed when the awning is already closed.

The flow has been designed as a collection of independent modules that communicate through MQTT, Link nodes and reusable subflows.

---

# 🏗️ Architecture

```text
                   ☀️ SunRain Shades

           Dashboard
                │
                ▼
      ☀️ SunRain Awning Control
                │
                ├──────────────► ESPSomfy RTS
                │
                ▼
      ⚙️ Motor Running Detection
                │
                ▼
           Dashboard

                ▲
                │
         🌦️ Buienradar
                │
                ▼
           🌧️ Rain Alert
                │
         🚦 Message Gate
                │
                ▼
     📡 HA + WhatsApp Notification
```

---

# 📦 Flow Modules

## ☀️ SunRain Awning Control

Responsible for:

- Manual awning control
- MQTT communication with ESPSomfy RTS
- Persistent awning position
- Dashboard controls

---

## ⚙️ HomeWizard Motor Running Detection

Responsible for:

- Motor running detection
- Communication monitoring
- LOCKED detection
- Dashboard motor status

---

## 🌧️ Rain Alert

Responsible for:

- Rain forecast monitoring
- Rain warning generation
- Dry notification
- Intelligent notification suppression

---

# 🔗 Reusable Subflows

The flow uses the following reusable components:

| Subflow | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| 🚦 Message Gate | Enables or suppresses rain warnings. |
| 📡 HA + WhatsApp Notification | Delivers notifications to Home Assistant and WhatsApp. |

---

# 🌐 External Systems

The flow communicates with:

- ESPSomfy RTS
- MQTT Broker
- HomeWizard Energy Socket
- Buienradar Rain Forecast
- Home Assistant
- WhatsApp Bridge

---

# 🎯 Design Principles

This flow has been designed around the following principles:

- Modular architecture
- Reusable subflows
- Persistent state where required
- Clear separation of responsibilities
- MQTT-first communication
- Dashboard-oriented operation
- Fail-safe behaviour
- Self-documenting components

---

# 📜 Revision History

| Version | Date | Changes |
|---------|------|---------|
| **1.0** | 2026-07-04 | Initial flow documentation and architecture overview. |

name: ESPSomfy RTS
info:
# ☀️ SunRain Awning Control

**Module:** SunRain  
**Project:** myHome  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Author:** Roland van Dalen  
**Last Updated:** 2026-07-03

---

# ☀️ ESPSomfy RTS

The SunRain awning is controlled by an **ESPSomfy RTS** controller.

ESPSomfy RTS is an open-source hardware and software project developed by [rstrouse](https://github.com/rstrouse/ESPSomfy-RTS) that bridges **Somfy RTS (Radio Technology Somfy)** motors with modern home automation systems using MQTT, Home Assistant and web-based APIs.

This project uses the MQTT interface of ESPSomfy RTS for all awning control and position feedback.

---

## 🧠 Function

This flow provides complete control and monitoring of the SunRain awning.

Manual commands from the dashboard are translated into MQTT commands for the ESPSomfy RTS controller.

The reported awning position is continuously monitored and stored persistently. The stored position is shared with other automation flows, such as the **Rain Alert** system, allowing them to make decisions based on the current awning position.

To prevent incorrect position updates immediately after a Node-RED deploy, the initial MQTT position message is suppressed before updating the stored position.

---

## 📥 Inputs

### Dashboard Commands

Manual control buttons:

- UP
- STOP
- DOWN
- 25%
- 50%
- 75%

Published MQTT topics:

```text
sunrain/shades/1/direction/set
sunrain/shades/1/target/set
```

---

### Awning Position

MQTT topic:

```text
sunrain/shades/1/position
```

Example payload:

```text
50
```

---

## 📤 Outputs

The flow provides:

### Dashboard

- Current awning position

### Flow Context

Updates the persistent variable:

```javascript
flow.set("sunrainAwningPosition", position, "file");
```

### Link Out

Provides the current awning position to other flows, including:

- Rain Alert
- Future automation flows

---

## 🔄 Processing

### Manual Control

Dashboard button presses publish MQTT commands directly to the ESPSomfy RTS controller.

---

### Position Monitoring

The reported awning position is received from ESPSomfy RTS via MQTT.

To prevent incorrect updates immediately after deployment, the first MQTT position message is ignored using an **RBE (Suppress Initial Value)** node.

Subsequent position updates are considered valid.

---

### Persistent Position Storage

Each valid position update is stored persistently.

The stored position is used to:

- update the dashboard
- control the Rain Alert Message Gate
- provide a reliable awning state after Node-RED restarts
- share the current position with other automation flows

---

## 💾 Flow Context

### Owned Variables

| Variable | Type | Store | Description |
|----------|------|-------|-------------|
| `sunrainAwningPosition` | Number | file | Last known awning position (0–100%). Persistently stored and shared with other flows. |

### Referenced Variables

This flow does not reference flow context variables owned by other groups.

---

## 🔗 Dependencies

### ESPSomfy RTS

Provides:

- MQTT command interface
- Position feedback
- RTS communication with the Somfy motor

---

### Message Gate (Rain Alert)

Consumes the persistent awning position to enable or suppress rain notifications.

---

### MQTT Broker

Provides communication between Node-RED and the ESPSomfy RTS controller.

---

## ⚙️ Configuration

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| Position topic | `sunrain/shades/1/position` | Reports the current awning position. |
| Direction topic | `sunrain/shades/1/direction/set` | Controls UP, STOP and DOWN commands. |
| Target topic | `sunrain/shades/1/target/set` | Sets the desired awning position (0–100%). |
| Initial MQTT suppression | Enabled | Prevents incorrect position updates immediately after deployment. |

---

## 📊 Dashboard

The dashboard provides:

- UP button
- STOP button
- DOWN button
- 25%, 50% and 75% preset position buttons
- Current awning position (%)

---

## 🧩 Design Goals

- Simple and intuitive awning control
- Reliable MQTT communication with ESPSomfy RTS
- Persistent position storage across Node-RED restarts
- Protection against invalid startup position reports
- Centralized position information for reuse by other automation flows
- Clear separation of control, monitoring and state management
- Easily reusable in other Somfy RTS installations

---

## 📜 Revision History

| Version | Date | Changes |
|---------|------|---------|
| **1.0** | 2026-07-03 | Initial documentation. Added module structure, persistent position storage, dependency overview, flow context documentation and design goals. |

name: HW Motor running detect
info:
# ⚙️ HomeWizard Motor Running Detection

**Module:** SunRain  
**Project:** myHome  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Author:** Roland van Dalen  
**Last Updated:** 2026-07-03

---

## 🧠 Function

The SunRain Somfy motor does not provide a status signal indicating whether it is running.

This flow determines the motor state by monitoring the power consumption of a dedicated HomeWizard Energy Socket. While the motor is operating it consumes approximately **200 W**, allowing reliable detection of whether the motor is **RUNNING** or **STOPPED**.

The flow also detects communication failures with the HomeWizard device. If the Somfy motor's safety switch disconnects the power, the HomeWizard API becomes unreachable. Instead of displaying an incorrect motor status, the dashboard reports the motor as **LOCKED**.

---

## 📥 Inputs

### Poll Timer

The HomeWizard API is polled every **2 seconds**.

### HomeWizard API

```text
GET http://192.168.1.34/api/v1/data
```

Example response:

```json
{
    "active_power_w": 198
}
```

---

## 📤 Outputs

The flow produces one of the following motor states:

| State | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **RUNNING** | Motor is operating. |
| **STOPPED** | Motor is idle. |
| **LOCKED** | HomeWizard Energy Socket is unreachable. |

Additional output:

```javascript
msg.power
```

contains the measured motor power in Watts and can be used by other automation flows.

---

## 🔄 Processing

### Motor State Detection

The measured motor power is compared with a configurable threshold.

| Measured Power | Motor State |
|----------------|-------------|
| > 50 W | RUNNING |
| ≤ 50 W | STOPPED |

A successful API response also resets the communication error counter.

---

### Communication Failure Detection

Communication failures from the HomeWizard API are monitored using a **Catch** node.

Each failed request increments a communication error counter.

After **two consecutive failures**, the flow assumes the HomeWizard Energy Socket has become unreachable (typically because the Somfy safety switch has disconnected the motor power).

The dashboard status changes to:

```text
LOCKED
```

The error counter is automatically reset after the next successful API response.

---

## 💾 Flow Context

### Owned Variables

| Variable | Type | Store | Description |
|----------|------|-------|-------------|
| `hwErrors` | Number | memory | Counts consecutive HomeWizard communication failures. Reset after a successful API response. Used to determine when the motor should be reported as **LOCKED**. |

### Referenced Variables

This flow does not reference flow context variables owned by other groups.

---

## 🔗 Dependencies

### HomeWizard Energy Socket

Provides:

- Real-time motor power measurement
- HTTP API used for polling

---

### Dashboard

Displays the current motor status:

- RUNNING
- STOPPED
- LOCKED

---

### HomeWizard API

Provides the measured motor power used to determine the motor state.

---

## ⚙️ Configuration

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| Poll interval | 2 seconds | Interval between HomeWizard API requests. |
| Running threshold | 50 W | Minimum measured power required to report the motor as RUNNING. |
| Communication failures | 2 | Number of consecutive API failures before reporting LOCKED. |

---

## 📊 Dashboard

The dashboard displays the current motor status:

- **RUNNING** – Motor is moving.
- **STOPPED** – Motor is idle.
- **LOCKED** – HomeWizard Energy Socket is unreachable (motor power disconnected).

This provides immediate feedback about both motor activity and communication status.

---

## 🧩 Design Goals

- Reliable motor state detection without additional sensors.
- Reuse existing HomeWizard Energy Socket measurements.
- Detect motor power loss through communication failure.
- Prevent incorrect motor status when the safety switch disconnects power.
- Provide a simple and reusable motor state for dashboards and automation flows.
- Separate motor detection from motor control logic.

---

## 📜 Revision History

| Version | Date | Changes |
|---------|------|---------|
| **1.0** | 2026-07-03 | Initial documentation. Added module structure, communication failure detection, configuration overview, flow context documentation, dependency overview and design goals. |

name: Rain Alert
info:
# 🌧️ Rain Alert

**Module:** SunRain  
**Project:** myHome  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Author:** Roland van Dalen  
**Last Updated:** 2026-07-03

---

## 🧠 Function

This flow monitors the Buienradar rain forecast and generates notifications when rain is expected within a configurable alert window.

Rain warnings are only delivered when the **SunRain awning is open** (position > 0%), preventing unnecessary notifications when the awning is already retracted.

When the forecast changes back to dry, a single **"No rain expected anymore"** notification is sent, but only if a rain warning was previously delivered.

This flow therefore provides an intelligent rain notification system with automatic suppression of redundant messages.

---

## 📥 Inputs

### Rain Forecast

MQTT topic:

```text
weather/rain
```

Example payload:

```json
{
    "location": "myHome",
    "rainMin": 10,
    "firstRainMM": 0.01,
    "maxRainMM": 1.0
}
```

### Awning Position

The current awning position is supplied indirectly through the **Message Gate**, which is controlled by the **SunRain Awning Control** group.

| Position | Rain Warnings |
|----------|---------------|
| 0 % | Disabled |
| 1–100 % | Enabled |

---

## 📤 Outputs

### Output 1

Rain warning notifications.

These messages are forwarded to the **Message Gate**, which determines whether they should be delivered.

---

### Output 2

Dry notifications.

These messages bypass the **Message Gate**, but are only generated if a rain warning was actually delivered earlier.

---

## 🔄 Processing

### Rain Detection

The flow evaluates the incoming Buienradar forecast.

A rain warning is generated when:

- rain is expected within the configured threshold (currently **20 minutes**)
- no warning has already been generated for the current rain event

---

### Message Gating

Rain warnings are forwarded through the **Message Gate**.

If the awning is already closed (0%), the Message Gate suppresses the warning.

Only warnings that successfully pass the Message Gate are marked as delivered.

---

### Dry Detection

When the forecast changes to:

```text
rainMin = -1
```

the flow determines whether a rain warning was actually delivered.

If so, a single notification is generated:

```text
No rain expected anymore
```

This prevents repeated "dry" notifications after suppressed rain warnings.

---

## 💾 Flow Context

### Owned Variables

| Variable | Type | Store | Description |
|----------|------|-------|-------------|
| `rainState` | String | memory | Current rain event state (`rain` or `dry`). Prevents duplicate rain warnings during the same rain event. |
| `rainWarningActuallySent` | Boolean | memory | Indicates whether a rain warning successfully passed the Message Gate. Determines whether a corresponding dry notification should be generated. |

### Referenced Variables

This flow does not directly reference flow context variables owned by other groups.

---

## 🔗 Dependencies

### Message Gate

Purpose:

Suppresses rain warnings when the awning is already closed.

Configuration:

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `stateName` | `messageGate` |

---

### HA + WhatsApp Notification

Purpose:

Formats and delivers notifications to:

- Home Assistant Mobile App
- WhatsApp

---

### SunRain Awning Control

Provides the awning position that controls the Message Gate.

---

### Buienradar Rain Forecast

Provides the rain forecast published on:

```text
weather/rain
```

---

## ⚙️ Configuration

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| Rain alert threshold | 20 minutes | Maximum time before rain for generating a warning. |
| Dry condition | `rainMin = -1` | Indicates that no rain is expected anymore. |

---

## 📊 Dashboard

The flow updates the dashboard with:

- Forecast location
- Rain status
- Minutes until rain
- Initial rain intensity
- Peak rain intensity

---

## 🧩 Design Goals

- Early warning before rain starts.
- No duplicate rain warnings.
- No unnecessary notifications when the awning is already closed.
- One "No rain expected anymore" notification per rain event.
- Separation of rain detection, message gating and notification delivery.
- Reusable notification logic through dedicated subflows.
- Modular architecture suitable for future automation extensions.

---

## 📜 Revision History

| Version | Date | Changes |
|---------|------|---------|
| **1.0** | 2026-07-03 | Initial documentation. Added intelligent rain detection, Message Gate integration, dry notification logic, flow context documentation, dependency overview and design goals. |
